automatically checks for spelling errors when a document is loaded and whenever the document changes. However, if the document is edited before the initial spell check is finished, the operation is canceled, and errors are reported only for modifications made from that point forward.If more than 500 errors are detected during the initial spell check, shows only the first 500 errors, and then any errors detected as further modifications are made.
A high number of errors may indicate that the document language is set incorrectly.

Words detected as spelling errors are underlined with a jagged red line. If you right-click a word, a list of suggestions is displayed. You can select one of them to replace the word, or use the Ignore option to instruct to ignore all occurrences of that particular spelling error during the current editing session.

section.title: Disabling Automatic Spell Checking
section.p: To disable this feature, open the Preferences action from the More drop-down menu on the toolbar, then clear the Enable automatic spell checking option.

section.title: Language Used by the Spell Checker
section.p: If your document specifies the language in certain elements by using the xml:lang or lang attribute, the automatic spell checker uses that language to detect errors in the content of those elements. You can also configure the spell.check.options flag in a custom options file to specify a language for the spell checker to use when no xml:lang or lang attribute is present.
